newsitem.title: USA: Continental pilots say willing to strike.
newsitem.headline: Continental pilots say willing to strike.

text.p: The pilots at Continental Airlines Inc said Wednesday they are willing to strike for higher wages, but still are interested in negotiating an agreement with the country's fifth largest airline.
Union president Len Nikolai said the pilots "will do whatever necessary to get an industry standard contract."
"But the last thing we want to have happen is a strike. A strike means failure....we truly want peace, we just want an industry standard contract," Nikolai said.
Labor experts said a strike by the Independent Association of Continental Pilots remains a distant possibility.
Houston-based Continental said it is "highly confident that we'll reach an agreement with the pilots."
"The comments that are being made as part of their PR campaign do not reflect the progress being made at the bargaining table," a Continental spokesman said.
The pilots union previously said it aims to reach a labor agreement by October 1. Contract negotiations began April 2.
The pilots union conducted "informational picketing" in Newark on Wednesday to explain their position in labor negotiations with the airline.
The pilots contend that they are paid 60 percent below the industry average. The union declined to provide details about their wage and benefit demands.

Continental said the pilots' contract demands would cost $1.4 billion over three years. The airline said the union has not yet responded to its counter-proposal, which offered a 38 percent wage increase over three years.
The pilots said they want to resolve details such as staffing, hours of service and scheduling before tackling economic issues.
